enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Inter‑subject variability in autonomic reactivity causes the nonconformity scores to be systematically miscalibrated for high‑reactivity individuals.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Subjects with exaggerated sympathetic responses produce extreme physiological feature values that lie outside the training distribution, inflating the nonconformity measure and shrinking prediction sets.
possible_confounders: Baseline cardiovascular fitness (VO2 max) influencing HRV reactivity
Medication use (beta‑blockers, anticholinergics) altering autonomic gain
Time‑of‑day circadian effects on sympathetic tone
control_variables: Resting HRV and EDA baseline per subject
rival_explanations: High‑reactivity subjects simply have noisier signals, not a calibration issue
The taxonomy's coarse stress labels happen to correlate with reactivity
minimum_data_needed: Per‑subject baseline autonomic measures (resting HRV, EDA)
Nonconformity scores stratified by reactivity quantiles
Calibration and test set splits preserving subject independence
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Subjects with exaggerated sympathetic responses produce extreme physiological feature values that lie outside the training distribution, inflating the nonconformity measure and shrinking prediction sets. This effect is confounded by baseline fitness, medication, and circadian phase; controlling for resting autonomic baselines and medication status in the Mondrian taxonomy (e.g., adding reactivity strata) should reduce miscalibration.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added baseline autonomic measures as covariates and suggested reactivity‑aware stratification.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Sensor‑specific drift in the wrist‑worn EDA channel during prolonged recordings leads to biased nonconformity estimates for later trials.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Gradual electrode impedance increase reduces EDA amplitude, shifting the feature distribution relative to the calibration set and causing undercoverage for sessions recorded late in the protocol.
possible_confounders: Ambient temperature and humidity changes across the session
Skin hydration and sweat rate variability
Movement artifacts increasing with fatigue
control_variables: Electrode impedance logs (if available) or proxy: signal‑to‑noise ratio over time
rival_explanations: Late‑session undercoverage is due to habituation (H9) not sensor drift
Calibration set under‑represents late‑session conditions
minimum_data_needed: Time‑resolved EDA signal quality metrics per trial
Nonconformity scores per trial with trial order preserved
Environmental sensor logs
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Gradual electrode impedance increase reduces EDA amplitude, shifting the feature distribution relative to the calibration set and causing undercoverage for sessions recorded late in the protocol. Confounders include ambient temperature, skin hydration, and movement artifacts; controlling for trial‑wise signal quality metrics and environmental conditions in the nonconformity calculation (e.g., weighting or detrending) can isolate drift effects.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added signal quality and environmental controls; suggested detrending or quality‑weighted nonconformity.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Non‑stationary heart‑rate variability (HRV) dynamics across the stress‑recovery cycle violate the exchangeability assumption within Mondrian strata.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Rapid autonomic transitions create temporal dependence in residuals; the conformal algorithm treats each window as independent, underestimating prediction interval width for transitional periods.
possible_confounders: Breathing rate changes not captured by respiration belt
Postural shifts (sitting/standing) during protocol
Caffeine or nicotine use before recording
control_variables: Respiration rate and depth per window
rival_explanations: Transitional periods have fewer calibration samples (small‑stratum effect, H8)
Nonconformity score choice (H6) is inadequate for dynamic HRV
minimum_data_needed: Window‑level HRV features with temporal ordering
Autocorrelation of nonconformity residuals within subjects
Stratum‑specific calibration sample counts
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Rapid autonomic transitions create temporal dependence in residuals; the conformal algorithm treats each window as independent, underestimating prediction interval width for transitional periods. Confounders include breathing pattern, posture, and substance use; controlling for these via time‑aware stratification (e.g., adding transition‑phase bins) or using block‑conformal methods can restore exchangeability.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added physiological and behavioral confounders; proposed time‑aware stratification.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Mislabeling of self‑reported stress levels for a subset of participants introduces systematic label noise into the Mondrian categories.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Subjects who under‑report stress are placed in a low‑stress stratum while their physiological signals resemble high stress, causing the nonconformity distribution to be too narrow for that stratum.
possible_confounders: Social desirability bias varying by personality traits
Language or scale interpretation differences
Fatigue affecting self‑report accuracy in later trials
rival_explanations: Physiological signals are genuinely ambiguous for some subjects
Stratum definitions are too coarse (H1, H5)
minimum_data_needed: Per‑subject self‑report reliability metrics
Nonconformity distributions split by self‑report consistency
External validation labels for a subset
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Subjects who under‑report stress are placed in a low‑stress stratum while their physiological signals resemble high stress, causing the nonconformity distribution to be too narrow for that stratum. Confounders include personality‑driven response bias, scale interpretation, and fatigue; controlling for self‑report reliability scores and using objective stress markers to identify mislabeled trials can correct stratum assignments.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added personality and fatigue confounders; suggested reliability‑weighted stratification.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Insufficient representation of certain demographic sub‑groups (e.g., age > 50) in the calibration set leads to stratum‑specific undercoverage.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Mondrian taxonomy does not include age as a stratification variable; older subjects exhibit different baseline HRV and EDA ranges, making the shared nonconformity quantile too optimistic for them.
possible_confounders: Comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes) affecting autonomic function
Medication load increasing with age
Fitness level differences within age groups
rival_explanations: Age effect is mediated by fitness, not age per se
Small‑stratum bias (H8) because older subjects are few
minimum_data_needed: Demographic and clinical metadata for all subjects
Stratum‑wise coverage broken down by age deciles
Calibration set size per age‑stratum combination
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Mondrian taxonomy does not include age as a stratification variable; older subjects exhibit different baseline HRV and EDA ranges, making the shared nonconformity quantile too optimistic for them. Confounders include comorbidities, polypharmacy, and fitness; controlling for these via age‑aware strata or covariate‑adjusted nonconformity scores can mitigate undercoverage.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added clinical and fitness confounders; proposed age‑aware stratification.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: The choice of nonconformity score (e.g., softmax margin) is poorly aligned with the multimodal feature geometry for stress classification.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Margin‑based scores ignore correlation structure between ECG, EDA, and respiration features, producing overly confident scores for out‑of‑distribution multimodal patterns.
possible_confounders: Feature scaling differences across modalities
Missing modality patterns (e.g., respiration dropout)
Classifier architecture bias (e.g., CNN vs. RF)
control_variables: Alternative nonconformity scores (e.g., Mahalanobis distance, conformalized quantile regression)
rival_explanations: Undercoverage stems from distribution shift (H2, H7) not score choice
Small calibration set (H8) amplifies any score's variance
minimum_data_needed: Nonconformity scores computed with multiple candidate functions
Coverage comparison across scores per stratum
Feature correlation matrices per condition
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Margin‑based scores ignore correlation structure between ECG, EDA, and respiration features, producing overly confident scores for out‑of‑distribution multimodal patterns. Confounders include feature scaling, missing modalities, and classifier bias; controlling for these by standardizing modalities, imputing missing channels, and evaluating alternative nonconformity functions (e.g., Mahalanobis distance) can align the score with the true geometry.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added scaling, missingness, and classifier confounders; suggested alternative scores.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Batch effects from different recording days cause distribution shift that is not captured by the Mondrian condition labels.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Day‑specific ambient temperature and humidity alter skin conductance baseline, shifting the EDA feature distribution; the conformal predictor treats all days as exchangeable within a condition.
possible_confounders: Experimenter variability (different staff per day)
Equipment recalibration or firmware updates
Participant sleep quality the night before
control_variables: Day identifier and ambient sensor logs
rival_explanations: Day effects are actually habituation across days (H9)
Sensor drift within day (H2) masquerades as batch effect
minimum_data_needed: Day‑level metadata (temperature, humidity, experimenter)
Nonconformity scores grouped by day
Calibration/test splits that respect day boundaries
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Day‑specific ambient temperature and humidity alter skin conductance baseline, shifting the EDA feature distribution; the conformal predictor treats all days as exchangeable within a condition. Confounders include experimenter variability, equipment changes, and participant sleep; controlling for day‑level covariates in the taxonomy (e.g., day‑specific strata) or using batch‑effect correction on features can restore coverage.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added experimenter, equipment, and sleep confounders; proposed day‑aware stratification.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Finite‑sample estimation error of the conditional quantile in small strata leads to systematic undercoverage for rare stress levels.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Mondrian splits the calibration data into many condition‑subject strata; strata with few samples yield noisy quantile estimates that are biased low.
possible_confounders: Unequal stratum sizes due to unbalanced protocol design
High‑dimensional nonconformity scores increasing variance
Correlation between stratum size and subject reactivity (H1)
rival_explanations: Rare stress levels are genuinely harder to predict (distributional shift)
Label noise (H4) inflates apparent undercoverage in small strata
minimum_data_needed: Stratum‑wise calibration sample sizes and coverage
Bootstrap confidence intervals for quantile estimates
Simulation of quantile bias vs. sample size
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Mondrian splits the calibration data into many condition‑subject strata; strata with few samples yield noisy quantile estimates that are biased low. Confounders include unbalanced design, high‑dimensional scores, and correlation with reactivity; controlling for stratum size via minimum‑sample thresholds, pooling similar strata, or using regularized quantile estimation can reduce bias.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added design imbalance and reactivity correlation; suggested pooling and regularization.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Physiological habituation across repeated stress trials reduces signal discriminability, but the Mondrian taxonomy treats each trial as identically distributed.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: Repeated exposure attenuates EDA peaks and HRV reactivity, moving later‑trial feature vectors toward the non‑stress distribution while the nonconformity calibration remains based on early‑trial statistics.
possible_confounders: Fatigue accumulating across trials
Learning or anticipation effects
Time‑of‑day drift (later trials later in day)
rival_explanations: Sensor drift (H2) mimics habituation
Day‑level batch effects (H7) if trials span days
minimum_data_needed: Trial‑wise physiological feature trajectories
Nonconformity scores per trial order
Habituation curves (e.g., EDA peak amplitude vs. trial)
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: Repeated exposure attenuates EDA peaks and HRV reactivity, moving later‑trial feature vectors toward the non‑stress distribution while the nonconformity calibration remains based on early‑trial statistics. Confounders include fatigue, anticipation, and time‑of‑day; controlling for trial index in the taxonomy (e.g., trial‑aware strata) or modeling habituation trajectories in the nonconformity function can account for non‑stationarity.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added fatigue, anticipation, and time‑of‑day confounders; proposed trial‑aware stratification.

enriched_hypotheses.original_hypothesis: Correlated missingness in the respiration belt (e.g., motion artifacts) creates informative missingness that the conformal predictor ignores.
enriched_hypotheses.original_mechanism: When respiration data are missing during high‑movement stress periods, the imputed or omitted features shift the joint distribution; the nonconformity score computed on available modalities underestimates uncertainty.
possible_confounders: Movement intensity correlated with stress level
Imputation method bias (mean vs. model‑based)
Other modalities also missing simultaneously (e.g., ECG artifacts)
rival_explanations: Missingness is random and coverage loss is due to reduced feature set (H6)
Stress periods are inherently noisier, not missingness‑driven
minimum_data_needed: Missingness logs per modality per window
Movement intensity time series
Coverage comparison: complete‑case vs. imputed vs. missingness‑aware nonconformity
enriched_hypotheses.enriched_mechanism: When respiration data are missing during high‑movement stress periods, the imputed or omitted features shift the joint distribution; the nonconformity score computed on available modalities underestimates uncertainty. Confounders include movement‑stress correlation, imputation bias, and multi‑modality dropout; controlling for missingness indicators in the nonconformity score (e.g., adding missingness as a feature) or using missingness‑aware conformal methods can correct coverage.
enriched_hypotheses.enrichment_notes: Added movement correlation, imputation bias, and multi‑modality dropout; suggested missingness‑aware nonconformity.
